name: Iridescence
rationale: Clean-room WebGL port written from the one-line effect description only (no upstream source read): a dependency-free thin-film interference shader gives hero sections and feature panels an opal-like, colour-shifting backdrop, with a static multi-hue CSS gradient when WebGL is unavailable.

speed.description: Flow speed; 0 holds a still frame.

scale.description: Size of the undulation; larger gives finer ripples.

thickness.description: Film thickness: how many colour bands cross each swell.

hue.description: Rotates the whole palette, in degrees; also shifts the CSS fallback gradient.

sheen.description: Strength of the specular glint and rim light.

depth.description: How far the troughs darken, for a gem-like body.

interactive.description: Ease the glint toward the pointer while the surface is animating.

a11y: The injected canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; the host's content, reading order and focus behaviour are unchanged.
The surface runs from deep troughs to bright glints, so text on it should sit on its own dark scrim to keep 4.5:1 contrast (the demo does this).
The pointer only moves a highlight; no information or action depends on it, and no click or key is intercepted.
Reduced motion stops the shader loop and the fallback drift and shows one still frame; forced-colors mode hides the canvas and paints the host in Canvas/CanvasText.
